formal_object.rationale: Allowed and positive masks contain released labels; logits use the same fixed temperature.

operations_and_conditions.rationale: B02: Differentiate to obtain allowed mass minus positive-conditioned mass. Condition: Both finite partition sums are nonempty H06: The aggregate inside-log loss can favor an easy positive instead of equally supervising every positive. Condition: More than one unequal positive logit

derivation.rationale: Differentiating log sums gives (p_allowed-p_pos)/T, while outside-log SupCon gives (p_allowed-uniform_positive)/T.

assumptions.rationale: Every positive is released/known; unknown relevance is not a negative label. A has at least one valid positive; a nontrivial new comparison needs genuine multiple positives. Candidate identities and labels stay unchanged in the native test scorer. These are conditional premises, not observed benchmark facts.

method_expression.rationale: The inside-log objective is implementable with nonempty labeled masks. Original multi-positive availability remains empirically unobserved.

prediction_and_falsifier.rationale: The aggregate loss weights each positive in proportion to its current positive-only softmax; easy positives can dominate, unlike uniform-target SupCon. Falsification: No released multi-positive rows collapses the distinction. Uniform-target SupCon performing as well or better at identical information/cost defeats the proposed necessity.

closest_alternative.rationale: SupCon Eq.3 is the same family up to a label-count constant; Eq.2 and a fair single-positive treatment are stronger alternatives than treating other known positives as negatives. This check only reviews the stated mathematical comparison; exhaustive full-text/author-code/native collision and originality decisions remain pending.
